summary: BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT: Powell Industries is a Houston engineer-to-order manufacturer of medium-voltage switchgear and factory-built power rooms that has been re-rated by the AI data-center build — it booked roughly $800 million of data-center infrastructure awards in the first nine months of FY2026, including a single order exceeding $400 million that it calls the largest in its history, and its backlog rose 69% year on year to $2.4 billion at 2026-06-30 on a 3.0x book-to-bill in that quarter alone. BACKGROUND. Founded 1947, Delaware-incorporated, listed on Nasdaq (POWL), 3,143 full-time employees at 2025-09-30. FY2025 (year ended 2025-09-30) revenue was $1,104.3M (+9%) with gross margin 29.4% and net income $180.7M (+21%), per the Form 10-K. It executed a three-for-one forward stock split effective 2026-04-02, so pre-split and post-split per-share figures cannot be compared without adjustment. Powell gives no numeric guidance, discloses backlog only to the nearest $0.1 billion, and names no customers in any filing — the $400M-plus data-center counterparty is unidentified in every public source.
ecosystemRole: The medium-voltage switchgear specialist in a market whose top five suppliers — ABB, Siemens, Schneider Electric, Eaton and GE Vernova — control roughly 55-60% of North American volume. Mordor Intelligence places Powell outside that oligopoly, among the regional specialists eroding its share through rapid customization and domestic production, and names its differentiator explicitly: tailored switchgear in ten weeks from its Texas facility, credited with winning multiple 2025 data-center awards. In an equipment market where lead times run in the tens of weeks and longer, that is not a price advantage but a schedule one. Its data-center scope is explicitly the outside-the-building electrical kit for behind-the-meter on-site generation — the switchgear between a campus's own generation and its halls — rather than the UPS and distribution inside them.

productsAndServices.name: PowlVac and PowlVac-AR metal-clad switchgear
productsAndServices.description: The core franchise: 5 kV and 15 kV class ANSI metal-clad switchgear combining Powell-designed and Powell-fabricated vacuum circuit breakers with Powell-built structures, in standard and arc-resistant construction. Built to ANSI C37.04, C37.06 and C37.20.2 with NEMA SG5, and arc-resistant variants tested to C37.20.7.
highlights: Continuous ratings 1200 A to 3000 A, and 4000 A with compartment-mounted forced-air cooling; interrupting 25 kA to 63 kA; three-cycle vacuum breakers with a K factor of 1

Arc-resistant construction available to IEEE accessibility Type 2C — the company states Type 2C meets the Type 2B requirements and goes beyond them, rated 40 kA rms symmetrical maximum for 0.5 seconds at 5/15 kV
On-Board Racking places the operator entirely outside the arc-flash zone using a digital HMI, with no external racking device required
3000 A and 2000 A breakers are interchangeable in a 1200 A cell, so an operator stocks one spare rating instead of several
Main bus can be rated to 174 kA peak for generator applications; all PowlVac breakers carry UL and C-UL labels as standard
In Type 2C designs the main bus compartment is segregated into a full-height bolt-on component rather than forming part of the rear cell assembly as in Type 2B
productsAndServices.positioning: The FY2025 10-K names the principal competitors as ABB, Eaton, Schneider and Siemens Industries, Inc. Mordor Intelligence places those same majors in a top five holding roughly 55-60% of North American medium-voltage switchgear and puts Powell in the specialist tier competing on customization and a ten-week lead time from Texas. Powell has no stated cost advantage and concedes competitors may have lower cost structures or a more favourable geographic footprint.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Direct to the end user or to the EPC firm acting for the end user, typically on competitive bid.
targetSegments: Commercial and other industrial including data centers
productsAndServices.roadmap: The company states it is leveraging its vacuum circuit breaker expertise to develop new products for a broader range of applications and sectors, and names hydrogen production, carbon capture, biofuels and sustainable aviation fuel as expansion targets.

productsAndServices.name: PowlVac-ND, PowlVac 38 and Power/Vac
productsAndServices.description: Three further metal-clad families: PowlVac-ND narrow-design gear for space-constrained rooms and as a direct replacement for obsolete air-magnetic lineups; PowlVac 38 at 27 kV and 38 kV; and Power/Vac, the legacy ANSI medium-voltage line Powell acquired from GE Consumer & Industrial in 2006.
highlights: PowlVac-ND is 26 inches wide at 5 kV with breakers at 1200 A or 2000 A and 36 kA or 50 kA interrupting, and 36 inches wide at 27/29.8 kV — against a 36-inch standard cell, the narrow design is what allows a retrofit into an existing room
PowlVac 38, introduced 1995, uses an axial-magnetic vacuum interrupter with copper-chrome contacts, fully qualified at KEMA for 40 kA interrupting duty and back-to-back capacitor switching
Power/Vac spans 5 kV, 8.25 kV and 15 kV at 20 kA to 63 kA and 1200 A to 4000 A, with 11-gauge steel compartment segregation and seismic qualification to IEEE 693 and IBC Zone 4 by shake-table test

Power/Vac safety options include reduced-energy let-through maintenance switches, arc-flash sensing relays, infrared thermal scanning windows, BriteSpot onboard thermal monitoring and onboard partial-discharge sensing

Roll-in vacuum replacement breakers exist for most major manufacturers' obsolete air-magnetic designs, including Westinghouse DH and DHP, Federal Pacific DST, Allis-Chalmers and Siemens type MA, ABB type ITE-HK, and GE Magneblast
productsAndServices.positioning: The replacement-breaker and retrofit business is a structural annuity on an installed base Powell did not originally supply — it competes for the second half of a forty-year asset's life against the original manufacturer.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Direct and through EPC firms; retrofit and replacement sold direct to owners and operators.

productsAndServices.name: Integrated package solutions — Power Control Rooms, e-houses and modules
productsAndServices.description: Factory-built, factory-tested electrical rooms shipped to site as walk-in enclosures: Power Control Rooms introduced in 1968, PCR-R e-houses on a rigid frame and structural steel skid, multi-story custom offshore power modules, Power Control Aisles, mobile substations and Substation Control Centers.
highlights: Custom engineered modules, including multi-story offshore power modules, are built at Powell's 64-acre Jacintoport facility on the Houston Ship Channel — the shipping-channel frontage is what makes very large modules transportable at all

PCRs use an interlocking panel design on a structural skid base, insulated to site-specific seismic requirements, shipped as one piece or multi-split with power and control interconnects already installed
E-houses are factory tested to UL, IEEE, CSA and NEMA standards before shipment
Blast-resistant equipment rooms and a High-Velocity Hurricane Zone variant are offered — the enclosure is engineered to the site's hazard, not just to the equipment
Substation Control Centers cover relay rooms, SCADA panels, UPS and DC systems and server racks for utility substations including air-insulated, gas-insulated, battery-storage and solar sites
A $12.4 million Jacintoport expansion adds 335,000 sq ft of laydown yard — a 62% increase — and doubles the shoreline bulkhead to 1,150 feet for multiple ship lanes
productsAndServices.positioning: SNS Insider names Powell among five companies shaping e-house technology alongside ABB, Siemens, Schneider Electric and Eaton, describing its position as designing custom-built systems requiring little site work. That framing is oil-and-gas-centric and predates the FY2026 data-center pivot.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Direct and through EPC firms, usually as part of a larger electrical scope.
productsAndServices.roadmap: The Jacintoport expansion was to begin construction in Q1 FY2026 and complete in the second half of FY2026; management stated it represents roughly $100 million of incremental annualized revenue when fully utilized.

productsAndServices.name: Low-voltage switchgear, switchboards and motor control
productsAndServices.description: FlexGear low-voltage metal-enclosed switchgear built as a universal platform accepting other manufacturers' draw-out breaker elements, FlexBoard UL 891 switchboards, PowlGear ME reduced-footprint metal-enclosed medium-voltage gear, and the FlexTrol and MVMCC-AR motor-control lines.
highlights: FlexGear accommodates Eaton Magnum DS, Siemens WL or Schneider Masterpact MTZ draw-out air circuit breaker elements in one Powell-engineered structure — Powell sells the assembly and the engineering, and buys the interrupting element from the companies its 10-K names as competitors
FlexGear main bus to 5000 A with bus bracing to 100 kAIC, in standard and arc-resistant construction
FlexBoard is a UL 891 switchboard at 480 V maximum, 1600 A to 5000 A, with short-circuit ratings up to 150 kA
FlexTrol medium-voltage motor control accepts either Eaton draw-out or Allen-Bradley fixed-mounted contactors in the same cubicle, in 400 A two-high and 800 A one-high designs at 5 kV and 7.2 kV

MVMCC-AR integrated arc-resistant motor control is IEEE Type 2 rated at 2300 / 4160 / 7200 V with 400 A and 800 A vacuum contactors, main bus to 4000 A braced to 50 kA, and close-couples to the switchgear lineup with no transition section
productsAndServices.positioning: The universal-platform strategy is unusual and commercially revealing: rather than compete on the breaker, Powell competes on the assembly, the engineering and the arc-resistant structure around whichever breaker the customer's standards already specify.

productsAndServices.name: Bus systems and DC switchgear
productsAndServices.description: Cable bus, non-segregated phase bus duct, segregated phase bus duct, isolated phase bus duct and DC duct; plus DC switchgear, high-speed DC breakers and semiconductor rectifiers for transit traction power, a market Powell entered in 1992.
highlights: Cable bus carries insulated copper or aluminium conductors at up to 38,000 V and up to 5,000 A, CSA certified to C22.2 numbers 27 and 201
Isolated phase bus duct runs 600 A to 42 kA at up to 38 kV with 110-150 kV BIL, for direct generator-to-transformer connection at utility and cogeneration plants
DC switchgear is designed and tested to IEEE C37.14, C37.16, C37.20.1 and IEEE 693, rated 4000 A to 8000 A at 800 VDC to 1600 VDC
Powell uses the Brush type NDC high-speed circuit breaker in all its DC switchgear designs, with a stated service life design beyond 30 years and fully bi-directional interruption
Semiconductor rectifiers are offered in medium, heavy and extra-heavy duty cycles and the company states they are adaptable to electrolyzer designs for clean hydrogen production
The NDC remote racking device operates from 25 feet away on existing 125 VDC cubicle control power
productsAndServices.positioning: Traction power is a small but genuinely differentiated line — Powell supplied more than 30 traction power substations with PowlVac-ND 27 kV arc-resistant switchgear and PCR e-houses for the 67-kilometre Réseau express métropolitain in Montreal, for CDPQ Infra and NouvLR.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Direct to transit authorities and their contractors.
productsAndServices.roadmap: Rectifier adaptation to electrolyzers is the stated hydrogen-adjacent path.

productsAndServices.name: Services, automation and EPiC
productsAndServices.description: Powell Global Services covers retrofit, retrofill, equipment upgrades, bus duct repair and refurbishment, start-up and commissioning, breaker life-extension, training, spares and parts-on-demand. Powell EPiC provides engineering, procurement, integration and construction. The Powell Automation Division supplies protection settings, control schemes and SCADA.
highlights: EPiC covers conceptual design, power-system analysis, relay coordination, procurement, demolition, logistics, lifting and setting in place, commissioning and start-up — the whole scope around the equipment
The Automation Division performs load-flow studies, short-circuit analysis and protection settings, and builds transfer, load-shed and paralleling control schemes
Power System Asset Management is delivered through Powell's own enterprise software with a single HMI combining SCADA and system health, which the company calls SCADA-H
Remsdaq Limited of Deeside, UK, maker of SCADA remote terminal units for substation control and automation, was acquired in August 2025 for £13.6 million / $18.4 million
Management stated on the Q3 FY2026 call that the Remsdaq integration has allowed the company to use its own automation boxes in data-center designs
productsAndServices.positioning: The services and automation layer is what converts a switchgear sale into a relationship over a forty-year asset life, and the Remsdaq acquisition is the company buying the intelligence layer rather than partnering for it.
targetSegments: Existing installed base across all end markets
productsAndServices.roadmap: Expansion of the automation platform through Remsdaq is a stated direction.

recentDevelopments.headline: Cantor Fitzgerald cuts its price target to $235 from $320 and keeps a Neutral rating after a call with the CFO, reiterating $235 on 2026-09-02
recentDevelopments.read: The de-rating logic is subtle and worth reading precisely: Cantor removed execution risk — stating that executing the $2.4bn backlog does not depend on the next major capacity addition — and in doing so removed the growth-capex optionality from the multiple.

recentDevelopments.headline: Q3 FY2026 Form 10-Q discloses approximately $800 million of data-center infrastructure project awards in the first nine months of FY2026, and adds new risk-factor language that data-center work will likely require less custom engineered-to-order equipment
recentDevelopments.read: The risk factor is the most important new sentence in the filing: the mix that is driving the order book is also the mix that is least like the engineered-to-order work carrying the 29-31% gross margin the whole re-rating rests on.

recentDevelopments.headline: Q3 FY2026 (quarter ended 2026-06-30): revenue $311.7M (+8.9%), gross margin 30.6%, net income $52.2M, diluted EPS $1.42; record new orders $934M (+158%), book-to-bill 3.0x, record backlog $2.4bn (+69% year on year)
recentDevelopments.read: Three mega orders landed in one quarter — the >$400M data center order, roughly $75M in petrochemical fertilizer and roughly $60M in US Gulf Coast LNG — while petrochemical revenue fell 49%, so the order book and the revenue line are telling different stories about which end market Powell is in.

recentDevelopments.headline: Quarterly cash dividend of $0.09 per share declared, payable 2026-09-16 to holders of record 2026-08-19
recentDevelopments.read: A post-split dividend on a debt-free balance sheet carrying $633.6M of cash and short-term investments — the capital return is immaterial next to the cash pile, which is being held for capacity.

recentDevelopments.headline: Compensation and Human Capital Committee approves a special one-time award of 36,000 restricted stock units to CEO Brett A. Cope, vesting 25% / 25% / 50% on 2027-07-01, 2028-07-01 and 2029-07-01
recentDevelopments.read: The 8-K states the award is designed to retain him past age-60 retirement eligibility under his 2016 employment agreement — a key-man retention action taken in the middle of the largest order cycle in the company's history.

recentDevelopments.headline: First disclosure of a mega data-center order with a value exceeding $400 million, awarded after the fiscal second quarter ended and described by the CEO as the largest order in Powell history, related to a behind-the-meter design of on-site generation assets
recentDevelopments.read: Powell won all of the outside electrical kit for the campus rather than sharing the scope, describes the configuration as a power island, and says the internal scope is not yet won — so the order is both a landmark and a bid for a second, larger one.

recentDevelopments.headline: Q2 FY2026 (quarter ended 2026-03-31): revenue $296.6M (+6%), gross margin 29.6%, net income $45.9M, diluted EPS $1.25; new orders $490M (+97%), backlog $1.8bn (+33%), book-to-bill 1.7x
recentDevelopments.read: Two mega orders were booked in the quarter itself, each above $75M, including what the company called the largest utility order it has ever recorded — the data-center order came after quarter-end and booked in Q3.

recentDevelopments.headline: Three-for-one forward stock split effected, with split-adjusted trading beginning 2026-04-06; authorized shares raised from 30 million to 90 million and shares outstanding from about 12.1 million to about 36.4 million
recentDevelopments.read: The split is the single largest source of misreading in this dossier: FY2023 to FY2025 per-share figures are pre-split and FY2026 quarters are post-split, and Powell has not restated the FY2025 10-K.

recentDevelopments.headline: Q1 FY2026 (quarter ended 2025-12-31): revenue $251.2M (+4%), gross margin 28.4%, net income $41.4M, diluted EPS $3.40 pre-split; new orders $439M (+63%), backlog $1.6bn, book-to-bill 1.7
recentDevelopments.read: This quarter contains the company's first megaproject booking in data centers at roughly $75M, with total data-center orders well in excess of $100M — the beginning of the mix shift that reshaped the backlog within three quarters.

recentDevelopments.headline: FY2025 (year ended 2025-09-30): revenue $1,104.3M (+9%), gross profit $324.4M at 29.4% (+19%), net income $180.7M (+21%), diluted EPS $14.86 pre-split; new orders $1.2bn (+9%), backlog $1.4bn
recentDevelopments.read: Q4 delivered record quarterly EPS of $4.22 pre-split on a 31.4% gross margin, and the stock fell more than 11% on the print — the first clear sign that expectations had moved ahead of the business.

recentDevelopments.headline: Powell UK Limited acquires Remsdaq Limited of Deeside, UK, maker of SCADA remote terminal units for substation control and automation, for £13.6 million / $18.4 million including $4.6M of cash acquired
recentDevelopments.read: Buying the automation layer rather than partnering for it; management stated on the Q3 FY2026 call that the integration lets Powell use its own automation boxes in data-center designs.

recentDevelopments.headline: Q3 FY2025 brought a $60 million electric utility award described as the largest utility order in Powell history at the time, more than $80 million combined from two offshore custom-module awards, and a $30 million US traction power order
recentDevelopments.read: Worth holding next to the FY2026 numbers: a $60M order was a company record in mid-2025, and nine months later a single data-center order exceeded $400M.

recentDevelopments.headline: $12.4 million Jacintoport investment announced, adding 335,000 sq ft of Power Control Room laydown yard — a 62% increase — and doubling the shoreline bulkhead to 1,150 feet for multiple ship lanes
recentDevelopments.read: The stated justification was anticipated oil and gas and LNG activity over three to five years, which is notable because the capacity it created is now absorbing data-center work instead.

recentDevelopments.headline: FY2024 (year ended 2024-09-30): revenue $1,012.4M, gross profit $273.1M at 27.0%, net income $149.8M, diluted EPS $12.29 pre-split; new orders $1.1bn
recentDevelopments.read: The base year for the current cycle, and the last one in which gross margin sat below 29% — the margin expansion from 27.0% to 29.4% to 30.6% is as much of the earnings story as the revenue growth.

recentDevelopments.headline: Powell acquires the medium-voltage ANSI switchgear product line from GE Consumer & Industrial for $32 million in cash, with an exclusive long-term commercial alliance to supply that channel's medium-voltage ANSI switchgear
recentDevelopments.read: The origin of the Power/Vac line and of Powell's installed-base service annuity. The GE unit involved later became GE Industrial Solutions and was divested to ABB — it is not GE Vernova, and the two are routinely confused.

relationships.note: Powell's own Form 10-K names ABB first among its principal competitors, and Mordor Intelligence places ABB in the top five controlling roughly 55-60% of the North America medium-voltage switchgear market.
relationships.context:
This is one of the few competitor links in the corpus stated by the company itself rather than inferred from a market report: the FY2025 10-K reads that Powell's principal competitors include ABB, Eaton, Schneider and Siemens Industries, Inc.

The relationship has two further threads. Powell publishes a PowlVac-ND replacement vacuum circuit breaker for the ABB type ITE-HK air circuit breaker, so it competes for the second half of an ABB installed base's life. And CEO Brett Cope spent twenty years at ABB, latterly as a Group Vice President responsible for ABB's global business with ExxonMobil.

relationships.via: Medium-voltage switchgear and low-voltage breaker elements
relationships.note: Named in Powell's 10-K as a principal competitor, and simultaneously a component supplier whose Magnum DS draw-out breakers and draw-out contactors Powell designs its FlexGear and FlexTrol platforms to accept.
relationships.context:
The dual relationship is the commercially interesting part. Powell's universal-platform strategy means it buys the interrupting element from a company it names as a competitor and sells the assembly, the engineering and the arc-resistant structure around it. FlexGear accommodates Eaton Magnum DS elements; FlexTrol medium-voltage motor control accepts Eaton draw-out contactors.

There is also a board-level link: director James W. McGill spent forty years at Eaton, retiring as President of the Electrical Sector for the Americas. Mordor Intelligence places Eaton inside the top five holding roughly 55-60% of North American medium-voltage switchgear, a tier Powell sits below.

relationships.via: Medium-voltage switchgear and low-voltage breaker elements
relationships.note: Named in Powell's 10-K as a principal competitor, and a component supplier whose Masterpact MTZ draw-out air circuit breaker elements the FlexGear platform is built to accept.
relationships.context:
Same dual structure as the Eaton relationship: named competitor in the filing, breaker supplier in the product literature. Powell publishes a dedicated instruction bulletin for FlexGear low-voltage switchgear equipped with Schneider, Siemens and Eaton breakers.

Mordor Intelligence puts Schneider in the top five controlling roughly 55-60% of the North American medium-voltage switchgear market and separately identifies its EcoStruxure Grid platform as part of a shift of competition toward software bundled with switchgear — the axis on which Powell's answer is the Remsdaq acquisition and its SCADA-H asset-management software.

relationships.note: Mordor Intelligence names General Electric (GE Vernova) among the five suppliers controlling roughly 55-60% of the North America medium-voltage switchgear market, in the same passage that places Powell in the specialist tier eroding that share.
relationships.context:
The ranking passage is the basis for this link and it is explicit: the top five suppliers — ABB, Siemens, Schneider Electric, Eaton and GE Vernova — control roughly 55-60% of the market, yet regional specialists are eroding share by offering rapid customization and domestic production, with Powell leveraging its Texas facility to deliver tailored switchgear in ten weeks and winning multiple 2025 data-center awards.

A caution that belongs with this link: Powell acquired its Power/Vac line from GE Consumer & Industrial in 2006, and that unit later became GE Industrial Solutions and was divested to ABB. It is not the GE Vernova business, and the 2006 transaction should never be read as a Powell–GE Vernova relationship.

relationships.note: Profiled alongside Powell Industries in Mordor Intelligence's North America medium-voltage switchgear company roster.
relationships.context:
Both companies are profiled in the same market study, outside the named top five. Hitachi Energy competes from a very different position — a global grid-equipment franchise with a stated multi-billion-dollar investment programme against Powell's roughly $1.16bn of revenue and single-country manufacturing base.

The overlap is partial. Hitachi Energy's centre of gravity is transformers and high-voltage equipment; Powell's is medium-voltage metal-clad switchgear and factory-built power rooms. They meet on a data-center campus rather than across a catalogue.

relationships.note: Mitsubishi Electric Power Products and Powell Industries are profiled alongside each other in Mordor Intelligence's North America medium-voltage switchgear company roster, and both appear in Straits Research's gas-insulated switchgear participant list.
relationships.context:
Both sit outside the five suppliers Mordor says control roughly 55-60% of the North American medium-voltage switchgear market, and both are pursuing the same domestic-capacity argument — Powell through a Texas plant and a ten-week quoted lead time, Mitsubishi Electric through an $86M advanced switchgear factory in the Pittsburgh region announced in 2024.

The overlap is real but partial in a way worth stating: metal-clad switchgear, which is Powell's core product class, is not a named Mitsubishi Electric Power Products product line, and gas-insulated switchgear at transmission voltages is not Powell's. They meet at the medium-voltage breaker rather than across the whole lineup.

relationships.note: Independent director Katheryn B. Curtis retired in 2022 as Senior Vice President, Generation at Dominion Energy Virginia, having previously served as Vice President Retail Operations and Vice President Merchant Operations at Dominion Energy.
relationships.context:
This is a board-biography link and not a commercial relationship. No source establishes Dominion Energy as a Powell customer, and Powell names no customers in any filing.

It is recorded because utility-sector governance experience is a real and sourced connection between the two covered companies, and because Powell's electric utility end market grew from 19% to 25% of revenue between FY2024 and FY2025 and accounted for 24% of backlog at 2026-06-30. Read it as domain experience on the board, nothing more.

policyExposure.exposure: Powell's raw materials are steel, copper and aluminium plus engineered electrical components, and material cost was 45% of revenue in FY2025, 47% in FY2024 and 49% in FY2023. Its own 10-K language states that ongoing and proposed changes to US trade policy, including the imposition of tariffs, could raise the cost of raw materials and engineered components and negatively affect margins, while saying it is not possible to predict the impact. Trade advisers describe a 2026 framework assessing duties on full customs value, with a capped 15% rate for specified metal-intensive industrial and electrical-grid equipment through 2027-12-31 rising to 25% from 2028. The exposure is two-sided: it raises Powell's input costs but penalises imported finished switchgear more heavily.
policyExposure.mitigation: Powell markets an explicit domestic-content position as a certified US manufacturer and registered GSA contractor, with equipment engineered and assembled in ISO-certified Texas facilities aligned to Buy American standards, and maintains parallel Buy Canadian and Buy UK positions for those markets. Its fixed-price contracts limit the ability to pass increases through, which the 10-K states directly.

policyExposure.exposure: Arc-resistant construction is a type-tested rating rather than a design claim, and the standard grades enclosures by which sides are protected and whether protection holds with a low-voltage compartment door open. Powell's arc-resistant products are rated to IEEE accessibility Type 2C at 40 kA rms symmetrical for 0.5 seconds at 5 and 15 kV, and 31.5 kA for 0.5 seconds on the 1200 A 38 kV design. The 2024 edition of the standard reclassified the document from a Guide to a Recommended Practice and its voltage ceiling rose from 38 kV to 52 kV between the 2007 and 2017 editions.
policyExposure.mitigation: The company states it actively participates in and chairs IEEE standards committees covering AC and DC switchgear, circuit breakers and arc resistance, and publishes its own technical bulletin series interpreting the standards, including comparisons of EEMAC and IEEE arc-resistant ratings.

policyExposure.regime: OSHA 29 CFR 1910 Subpart S and NFPA 70E
policyExposure.exposure: The workplace electrical-safety regime is the demand driver beneath Powell's arc-resistant franchise. NFPA 70E requires an energised-work justification, an arc-flash risk assessment, equipment labelling with incident energy and protective clothing matched to that number; OSHA revised its electrical standard to reference NFPA 70E and cites employers for non-compliance. Where switchgear is arc-resistant, the operating task's arc-flash PPE requirement changes materially — which is what converts arc-resistant construction from an option into a specification.
policyExposure.mitigation: Not applicable — the regime is a demand driver for Powell rather than a cost to be mitigated. Powell's products reference NFPA 70E in their arc-resistant instruction bulletins.

policyExposure.regime: Buy American and GSA federal procurement
policyExposure.exposure: Powell holds federal registrations including DUNS 00-807-4387, CAGE code 2M091 and ISO-9001, with product service codes 5925, 6110, 6130 and 6150, and markets itself as a registered GSA contractor with a dedicated government team. Note the company says Buy American rather than the specific Build America, Buy America regime, which it does not cite by name.
policyExposure.mitigation: Domestic manufacture in Texas is the mitigation and the marketing position simultaneously.

policyExposure.exposure: The FY2025 10-K notes the Act, signed 2025-07-04, and states that the company was evaluating its impact. Powell's effective tax rate was 23% in FY2025 and 24% in FY2024.
policyExposure.mitigation: No company statement beyond the evaluation disclosure was located.

financials.commentary: Powell reports in US dollars, so the normalized overlay is as reported with no conversion. Three honesty notes govern this record. First, the three-for-one forward stock split effected 2026-04-02 means FY2023 to FY2025 per-share figures are pre-split and FY2026 quarterly figures are post-split, and the company has not restated the FY2025 10-K — a multi-year EPS series that ignores this shows a false collapse in FY2026. Second, Powell issues no numeric guidance of any kind; the closest management has come in FY2026 is a statement that gross margins are expected to hold at levels consistent with the trailing twelve months, so every annual comparison above that carries a verdict is against analyst consensus rather than company guidance, and where no consensus was retrievable the field is left empty. Third, the outlets disagree on consensus figures for the same print — for Q3 FY2026 the EPS consensus was $1.49 at Zacks and MarketBeat and $1.47 at TheFly, and the revenue consensus ranged from $316.70M to roughly $318.2M — so each is named with its basis and none are blended. Zacks is explicitly an adjusted-EPS basis; TheFly and MarketBeat do not state theirs.

strategyRead: **(High confidence)** We assess that Powell's competitive advantage is schedule rather than price or technology. Basis: Mordor Intelligence places the top five suppliers — ABB, Siemens, Schneider Electric, Eaton and GE Vernova — at roughly 55-60% of the North America medium-voltage switchgear market and names Powell's differentiator explicitly as tailored switchgear in ten weeks from its Texas facility, credited with winning multiple 2025 data-center awards. Powell's own 10-K concedes competitors may have lower cost structures or a more favourable geographic footprint. In a market where equipment delivery sets the project date, a supplier who compresses lead time is selling a power-on date the buyer cannot otherwise obtain.

**(High confidence)** We assess the company has been structurally repriced by one order rather than by a trend, and that the concentration is the risk. Basis: a single data-center order exceeding $400M is more than 16% of the $2.4bn backlog on its own; the company describes roughly $800M of data-center awards across the first nine months of FY2026; and commercial and other industrial moved from 15% to 40% of backlog in three quarters. Powell itself frames the order as phase one of a multi-phase behind-the-meter campus whose later phases depend on execution of the first.

**(Moderate confidence)** We assess the mix shift that produced the order book also threatens the margin that justified the re-rating. Basis: the Q3 FY2026 10-Q introduces new risk-factor language that data-center work will likely require less custom engineered-to-order equipment, and Powell's gross margin expanded from 27.0% in FY2024 to 29.4% in FY2025 to 30.6% in the latest quarter on precisely the custom, engineered content that language says is diluting. Management's only forward statement is that margins should hold at trailing-twelve-month levels — which is a claim about the next year, not about the mix now entering the backlog.

**(Moderate confidence)** We assess the universal-platform strategy is a deliberate refusal to compete where Powell cannot win. Basis: FlexGear low-voltage switchgear is engineered to accept Eaton Magnum DS, Siemens WL or Schneider Masterpact MTZ draw-out elements, and FlexTrol accepts either Eaton draw-out or Allen-Bradley fixed-mounted contactors — so Powell buys the interrupting element from the companies its own 10-K names as principal competitors and sells the assembly, the engineering and the arc-resistant structure around whichever breaker the customer's standards already specify. It monetises the part of the product that is engineered per project rather than the part that is a catalogue item.

**(Low confidence)** We assess the analyst de-rating reflects a change in what the multiple was paying for rather than a change in the business. Basis: Cantor Fitzgerald cut its target from $320 to $235 on 2026-08-14 after a call with the CFO, on reasoning that the existing leased capacity provides the footprint needed to execute the current backlog and that the larger 275,000-300,000 sq ft facility supports growth beyond it — de-risking execution while removing growth-capex optionality. Whether that is the correct read of a $70-100M capital decision is not establishable from public sources, and the analyst panel covering Powell is thin, with targets spanning roughly $217 to $427.

**Collection gap — the counterparty to the largest order in the company's history is unknown and deliberately withheld.** No hyperscaler, developer, EPC, site or generation OEM is named in the Q2 or Q3 FY2026 releases, the 10-Q, or either earnings call, and no 8-K material-contract filing exists for it. The order is described only as a behind-the-meter design of on-site generation assets at gigawatt scale across multiple phases, delivered from at least five North American facilities on a roughly two to two-and-a-half year burn. This is a structural disclosure practice, not a research failure: the 10-K states that no single customer exceeded 10% of consolidated revenues in either FY2025 or FY2024, and Powell names no customers anywhere.

**Collection gap — no on-site generation partner is identified.** An order covering the outside electrical scope for a couple of gigawatts of behind-the-meter generation necessarily implies a prime-power OEM on the same campus, and no source names one. That is the single most valuable missing link in this dossier, because it would connect Powell to the gen-set and turbine vendors already covered elsewhere in this corpus.

**Collection gap — Powell has no trade-press coverage.** Targeted searching found no coverage in T&D World, EC&M, Data Center Frontier, Data Center Knowledge, Reuters or the Houston Chronicle across eighteen months. Powell is covered as a stock by financial media and market-research vendors, and not as an industry actor. Any reader expecting independent operational reporting on this company should know it does not exist.

**Entity caution.** Powell's 10-K names "Siemens Industries, Inc." as a principal competitor and its FlexGear literature cites Siemens WL breakers. That is the Siemens AG industrial business, not Siemens Energy AG, and no competitor link to the covered `siemens-energy` slug is asserted here on that basis. Separately, the Power/Vac line was acquired from GE Consumer & Industrial in 2006 — a unit that became GE Industrial Solutions and was divested to ABB, and is not GE Vernova.
